events.title: Orville Wright dies

events.title: The last quagga dies in Amsterdam's zoo

events.title: Florence Nightingale arrives at Scutari

events.title: The 'Great Stink' engulfs London

fact: Pong arrived in arcades just eight days before Apollo 17, the last crewed Moon mission, launched.

events.title: Tennis for Two is shown at a US lab open day

events.title: MIT students create the game Spacewar!

events.title: The Godfather premieres in New York

events.title: Atari releases Pong

events.title: Apollo 17 launches for the Moon

events.title: The Curies announce the discovery of radium

events.title: Hong Kong is handed back to China

fact: Napoleon and Wellington, the rival commanders at Waterloo, were born less than four months apart in 1769.

events.title: James Watt patents his separate condenser

events.title: Future Duke of Wellington is born

events.title: Captain Cook's crew observe the transit of Venus

events.title: Napoleon is born on Corsica

events.title: The Duke of Wellington dies
events.note: He died at Walmer Castle in Kent, aged 83.

fact: Dodos were still alive on Mauritius when the Taj Mahal was completed in 1653 — the last accepted sighting was in 1662.

events.title: Dutch sailors first describe the dodo

fact: Mother Teresa died on 5 September 1997, just five days after Princess Diana.

events.title: Charles and Diana marry at St Paul's

events.title: Mother Teresa dies in Calcutta

fact: The yacht America won the cup named after her in 1851, and the US then held it for 132 years until Australia II won in 1983.

events.title: Moby-Dick is published in London

events.title: Australia II wins the America's Cup

events.title: Handel dies in London

events.title: Wolfe defeats the French at Quebec

events.title: Arthur Guinness leases the St James's Gate brewery

events.title: Mamluks halt the Mongols at Ain Jalut

events.note: James Naismith nailed up peach baskets in Springfield.

events.title: The Nutcracker premieres in St Petersburg
events.note: Critics panned it; it is now a Christmas staple.

events.title: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky dies
events.note: He died nine days after premiering his Pathétique symphony.

fact: Japan's 47 ronin took their revenge in early 1703, four months before Peter the Great founded St Petersburg.

events.title: An earthquake sinks much of Port Royal, Jamaica
events.note: The pirate haven was called the “wickedest city on Earth”.

events.title: The 47 ronin avenge their master in Edo
events.note: They killed Kira Yoshinaka, then gave themselves up.

events.title: Peter the Great founds St Petersburg
events.note: He began with a fortress on Hare Island in the Neva.

events.title: England and Scotland unite as Great Britain
events.note: The Acts of Union created one parliament at Westminster.

events.title: Mount Fuji erupts for the last time
events.note: Ash fell on Edo, about 100 km away.

fact: Geronimo surrendered to the US Army less than eight weeks before the Statue of Liberty was dedicated.

events.title: Geronimo surrenders to the US Army
events.note: The Apache leader gave up at Skeleton Canyon, Arizona.

events.title: The Statue of Liberty is dedicated
events.note: President Grover Cleveland presided over the ceremony.

events.title: An earthquake devastates San Francisco
events.note: Fires burned for days and destroyed most of the city.

events.title: Geronimo dies
events.note: He died at Fort Sill, Oklahoma, still a prisoner of war.

events.title: Louis Blériot flies across the English Channel
events.note: The hop from Calais to Dover took about 36 minutes.

fact: Boston's deadly Great Molasses Flood struck one day before the US ratified Prohibition.

events.title: Patriots dump tea into Boston Harbor
events.note: The Boston Tea Party protested British taxes.

events.title: An armistice ends the fighting of World War I
events.note: It was signed in a railway carriage at Compiègne.

events.title: A wave of molasses floods Boston's North End
events.note: A burst tank sent a sticky wave through the streets, killing 21.

events.title: The Prohibition amendment is ratified
events.note: Nebraska was the 36th state, completing ratification.

events.title: The Treaty of Versailles is signed
events.note: Signed in the Hall of Mirrors, five years after Sarajevo.

fact: The internet's ancestor ARPANET sent its first message in October 1969, about ten weeks after Woodstock.

events.title: The Stonewall riots break out in New York
events.note: Police raided the Stonewall Inn in Greenwich Village.

events.title: Ted Kennedy's car crashes at Chappaquiddick
events.note: His passenger, Mary Jo Kopechne, drowned.

events.title: The Woodstock festival opens
events.note: Around 400,000 people came to a dairy farm in New York state.

events.title: ARPANET sends its first message
events.note: It crashed after the letters 'LO' of 'LOGIN'.

events.title: Sesame Street premieres
events.note: Big Bird and Oscar the Grouch appeared in the first episode.

fact: Starbucks opened in Seattle less than two months after an astronaut hit golf balls on the Moon.

events.title: Alan Shepard hits golf balls on the Moon
events.note: He used a six-iron head attached to a sampling tool on Apollo 14.

events.title: Joe Frazier beats Muhammad Ali at Madison Square Garden
events.note: It was billed as the "Fight of the Century"; Ali lost on points.

events.title: Starbucks opens in Seattle
events.note: It first sold coffee beans, not brewed drinks.

events.title: US table tennis players visit China
events.note: The trip, "ping-pong diplomacy", thawed US–China relations.

events.title: Jim Morrison of the Doors dies in Paris
events.note: He was found in his bathtub, aged just 27.

fact: Gun maker Beretta, still run by the same family, was selling barrels in 1526 — 17 years before Copernicus published.

events.title: Beretta sells gun barrels to Venice
events.note: The arsenal of Venice paid for 185 arquebus barrels.

events.title: Jacques Cartier sails into the Gulf of St Lawrence
events.note: He planted a cross on the Gaspé coast and claimed it for France.

events.title: Copernicus publishes his Sun-centred universe
events.note: He reportedly saw the printed book on his deathbed.

events.title: Nostradamus publishes his book of prophecies
events.note: Fans still claim its verses foretold later events.

events.title: The Spanish Armada sails against England
events.note: Storms wrecked much of the fleet on the way home.

fact: Hagia Sophia's great dome collapsed in 558, only about 20 years after the church was completed — it was rebuilt taller.

events.title: Hagia Sophia is dedicated in Constantinople
events.note: For centuries it was the largest church in the world.

events.title: Bubonic plague strikes Constantinople
events.note: The pandemic may have killed millions around the Mediterranean.

events.title: Hagia Sophia's main dome collapses
events.note: Earthquakes had weakened it; it was rebuilt higher.

events.title: Muhammad is born in Mecca
events.note: He was orphaned young and raised by his grandfather and uncle.

events.title: Augustine's mission lands in Kent
events.note: Sent from Rome by Pope Gregory to convert the Anglo-Saxons.

fact: Ramesses II died around 1213 BC — and in 1976 his mummy landed in Paris to full military honours fit for a king.

events.title: Egypt and the Hittites clash at Kadesh
events.note: Possibly the largest chariot battle ever fought.

events.title: Pharaoh Ramesses II dies after a 66-year reign
events.note: He outlived many of his own children.

events.title: Shelley publishes 'Ozymandias'
events.note: The sonnet mocks a shattered statue of Ramesses.

events.title: Abu Simbel's temples are moved to higher ground
events.note: They were cut into blocks to escape Lake Nasser.

events.title: Ramesses II's mummy is flown to Paris for treatment
events.note: Scientists treated it for a fungal infection.

fact: Hennig Brand discovered phosphorus by boiling urine in 1669 — three years after the Great Fire of London.

events.title: The Royal Society is founded in London
events.note: It began after a lecture by Christopher Wren.

events.title: Robert Hooke's Micrographia names the 'cell'
events.note: His drawings of a flea and a louse astonished readers.

events.title: The Great Fire of London breaks out
events.note: It started in a bakery on Pudding Lane.

events.title: Hennig Brand discovers phosphorus
events.note: The Hamburg alchemist was seeking the philosopher's stone.

events.title: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek sees single-celled life
events.note: He called the microbes 'animalcules'.

fact: Houdini was born weeks before the first Impressionist show opened — and died five weeks before Claude Monet.

events.title: Harry Houdini is born in Budapest
events.note: He was born Erik Weisz and grew up in Wisconsin.

events.title: The first Impressionist exhibition opens in Paris
events.note: Monet's Impression, Sunrise gave the movement its name.

events.title: Britain's General Strike begins
events.note: It lasted nine days before the unions called it off.

events.title: Harry Houdini dies
events.note: He died of peritonitis on Halloween in Detroit.

events.title: Claude Monet dies at Giverny
events.note: He painted water lilies in his garden there for decades.

fact: Russia's tsar freed the serfs on 3 March 1861 — the day before Abraham Lincoln was sworn in as president.

events.title: Work begins on the Suez Canal
events.note: Ferdinand de Lesseps struck the first blow at Port Said.

events.title: Dickens begins serialising A Tale of Two Cities
events.note: It ran in weekly parts in his magazine All the Year Round.

events.title: Garibaldi sails for Sicily with his Thousand
events.note: His red-shirted volunteers set off from near Genoa.

events.title: Russia's tsar frees the serfs
events.note: Alexander II's manifesto freed about 23 million people.

events.title: Abraham Lincoln is sworn in as president
events.note: Seven Southern states had already seceded.

fact: John Tyler was born 19 days before Benjamin Franklin died — yet one of his grandsons lived until May 2025.

events.title: Future President John Tyler is born
events.note: Born on a Virginia plantation; he became the tenth president.

events.title: Benjamin Franklin dies
events.note: He died in Philadelphia, aged 84.

events.title: President William Henry Harrison dies in office
events.note: He died a month after his inauguration, making Tyler president.

events.title: Pope Francis dies
events.note: He died at his Vatican residence the day after Easter Sunday.

events.title: President John Tyler's last living grandson dies
events.note: Harrison Ruffin Tyler was born when his father was 75.

fact: Neuschwanstein, the "fairy-tale castle", was begun more than six years after London's first Underground line opened.

events.title: London's first Underground railway opens
events.note: The Metropolitan Railway ran steam trains under the city.

events.title: Foundation stone of Neuschwanstein Castle is laid
events.note: King Ludwig II of Bavaria built it as a romantic retreat.

events.title: Outlaw Jesse James is shot dead at home
events.note: A gang member shot him in the back for the reward money.

events.title: Ludwig II of Bavaria is found drowned
events.note: He died in Lake Starnberg days after being declared insane.

events.title: Disneyland opens in California
events.note: Its Sleeping Beauty Castle was inspired by Neuschwanstein.

fact: Google is older than the euro: it was founded in September 1998, four months before the currency launched.

events.title: Europe's passport-free Schengen Area comes into being
events.note: Seven countries scrapped passport checks at their shared borders.

events.title: Netflix is founded
events.note: It began by renting DVDs by mail.

events.title: Google is founded
events.note: It started in a garage in Menlo Park, California.

events.title: The euro is launched
events.note: At first it existed only electronically.

events.title: Euro notes and coins enter circulation
events.note: Twelve countries swapped their old currencies at once.

fact: 53,000 fans watched a women's football match on Boxing Day 1920 — within a year England's FA had banned the women's game for 50 years.

events.title: Dick, Kerr Ladies draw a record crowd at Goodison Park
events.note: About 53,000 watched them beat St Helens Ladies 4–0 for charity.

events.title: England's FA bans women's football from its grounds
events.note: It declared the game "quite unsuitable for females".

events.title: The Anglo-Irish Treaty is signed
events.note: It led to the creation of the Irish Free State.

events.title: The FA lifts its ban on women's football
events.note: The Women's FA Cup had begun the same year.

events.title: England win the women's European Championship
events.note: Chloe Kelly scored the winner against Germany at Wembley.

fact: Television was first demonstrated in London just seven weeks before Goddard launched the first liquid-fuelled rocket.

events.title: Paul Nipkow patents a scanning disk for images
events.note: His spinning disk was the basis of mechanical TV.

events.title: John Logie Baird demonstrates television
events.note: He showed moving faces to scientists in Soho.

events.title: Robert Goddard launches a liquid-fuelled rocket
events.note: It flew for 2.5 seconds over a Massachusetts farm.

events.title: Winnie-the-Pooh is published
events.note: A. A. Milne based it on his son's toys.

events.title: The BBC starts a regular TV service
events.note: It broadcast from Alexandra Palace in London.

fact: Japan's Tale of Genji, often called the first novel, was written by a woman about 600 years before Don Quixote.

events.title: The Tale of Genji is circulating at Japan's court
events.note: Written by the lady-in-waiting Murasaki Shikibu.

events.title: England's Domesday Book survey is compiled
events.note: A record of who owned what across England.

events.title: Don Quixote is published in Madrid
events.note: Cervantes's knight tilted at windmills.

events.title: Robinson Crusoe is published
events.note: Defoe presented it as a true castaway's memoir.

events.title: Samuel Johnson's Dictionary is published
events.note: It took Johnson and his helpers about nine years.

fact: A 'Roman' embassy reached Han China in AD 166 — a year after the Antonine Plague broke out in Rome's empire.

events.title: Zhang Qian sets out on his mission to the west
events.note: His travels opened the routes later called the Silk Road.

events.title: Gan Ying is sent towards Rome but turns back
events.note: He was told the sea crossing could take two years.

events.title: The Antonine Plague breaks out
events.note: It may have killed millions across the Roman Empire.

events.title: A 'Roman' embassy reaches the Han court
events.note: The envoys claimed to come from 'Andun', thought to be Marcus Aurelius.

events.title: The Yellow Turban Rebellion erupts in China
events.note: The revolt fatally weakened the Han dynasty.

fact: Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift in January 1912 — weeks before Arizona became a US state.

events.title: Ortelius suggests the continents were once joined
events.note: The Flemish mapmaker noticed how the coastlines matched.

events.title: Alfred Wegener proposes continental drift
events.note: He presented the idea at a geology meeting in Frankfurt.

events.title: Arizona becomes a US state
events.note: It was the last of the contiguous 48 states to join.

events.title: Piltdown Man is unveiled in London
events.note: The 'missing link' skull was exposed as a forgery in 1953.

events.title: Wegener dies on the Greenland ice sheet
events.note: His body was found the following spring.

fact: Superman reached newsstands in April 1938 — more than six months before Orson Welles's Martian invasion broadcast.

events.title: Germany annexes Austria
events.note: German troops crossed the border unopposed.

events.title: Superman debuts in Action Comics #1
events.note: Two Cleveland teenagers had created the character.

events.title: Orson Welles broadcasts The War of the Worlds
events.note: The radio drama was staged as live news bulletins.

events.title: Kristallnacht pogrom sweeps Germany
events.note: Nazi mobs wrecked Jewish shops and synagogues.

events.title: Hahn and Strassmann split the uranium atom
events.note: Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch explained it as fission.

fact: British troops seized Benin City and its bronzes just four months before Queen Victoria's Diamond Jubilee.

events.title: British troops capture Benin City
events.note: Thousands of Benin Bronzes were carried off to Europe.

events.title: Oscar Wilde is released from prison
events.note: He left for France that night and never returned to Britain.

events.title: Queen Victoria celebrates her Diamond Jubilee
events.note: She marked 60 years on the throne with a London procession.

events.title: Andrée’s balloon sets off for the North Pole
events.note: The crew’s bodies were found on an Arctic island 33 years later.

events.title: The First Zionist Congress meets in Basel
events.note: Theodor Herzl called for a Jewish homeland.

fact: Elizabeth II's first prime minister, Churchill, was born in 1874; her 15th, Liz Truss, took office two days before she died.

events.title: Winston Churchill is born at Blenheim Palace
events.note: Born into the aristocratic Spencer-Churchill family.

events.title: Princess Elizabeth becomes queen
events.note: She was in Kenya when her father, George VI, died.

events.title: Winston Churchill wins the Nobel Prize in Literature
events.note: Honoured for his histories and his speeches.

events.title: Liz Truss becomes prime minister
events.note: The Queen appointed her at Balmoral; she lasted 49 days.

events.title: Queen Elizabeth II dies
events.note: She died at Balmoral Castle, aged 96.

fact: The British burned the White House only 14 years after its first resident, John Adams, moved in.

events.title: John Adams moves into the White House
events.note: It was still unfinished when the president arrived.

events.title: Pride and Prejudice is published
events.note: Jane Austen's novel appeared anonymously.

events.title: Napoleon arrives in exile on Elba
events.note: He was allowed to rule the small island as its sovereign.

events.title: British troops burn the White House
events.note: The Capitol was set alight the same night.

events.title: Francis Scott Key writes "The Star-Spangled Banner"
events.note: He watched the bombardment of Fort McHenry from a ship.

fact: New Horizons was launched toward the planet Pluto in January 2006; seven months later, Pluto was no longer a planet.

events.title: The first YouTube video is uploaded
events.note: 'Me at the zoo' lasts 19 seconds.

events.title: New Horizons launches toward Pluto
events.note: It carries some of Clyde Tombaugh's ashes.

events.title: Twitter launches to the public
events.note: Posts were limited to 140 characters.

events.title: Pluto is reclassified as a dwarf planet
events.note: The vote was held by the International Astronomical Union.

events.title: New Horizons flies past Pluto
events.note: It found a heart-shaped plain of nitrogen ice.

fact: Twinings began selling tea in London in 1706 — a year before the Kingdom of Great Britain existed.

events.title: Edward Lloyd's coffee house is open in London
events.note: Ship owners met at Edward Lloyd's coffee house to arrange insurance.

events.title: Thomas Twining opens his tea shop in London
events.note: Twinings still trades from the same site on the Strand.

events.title: England and Scotland unite as Great Britain
events.note: The Acts of Union created a single Parliament at Westminster.

events.title: The Boston Tea Party
events.note: Protesters dumped 342 chests of tea into Boston Harbor.

events.title: The tea clipper Cutty Sark is launched
events.note: She was built at Dumbarton for the China tea trade.

fact: Talking pictures arrived with The Jazz Singer just two days after carving began on Mount Rushmore.

events.title: Volvo builds its first car
events.note: The ÖV4 rolled out of a Gothenburg factory.

events.title: Philo Farnsworth transmits an electronic TV image
events.note: The 21-year-old's first image was a straight line.

events.title: Carving begins on Mount Rushmore
events.note: Gutzon Borglum led some 400 workers.

events.title: The Jazz Singer premieres
events.note: Al Jolson spoke: 'You ain't heard nothin' yet!'

events.title: Thomas Edison dies
events.note: He died at his home in West Orange, New Jersey.

fact: Iceland's Althing first met in 930 — 335 years before Simon de Montfort's famous parliament in England.

events.title: Norse settlers begin to settle Iceland
events.note: Ingólfr Arnarson is traditionally the first permanent settler.

events.title: Iceland's Althing assembly first meets
events.note: It gathered outdoors at Þingvellir each summer.

events.title: Iceland adopts Christianity at the Althing
events.note: The lawspeaker decided after lying under a cloak for a day.

events.title: Simon de Montfort's parliament meets
events.note: It summoned elected burgesses from the towns.

events.title: Iceland becomes an independent republic
events.note: It broke its last ties with Denmark during WWII.

fact: A British officer hunting a tiger found India's forgotten Ajanta Caves in April 1819 — less than a month before Queen Victoria was born.

events.title: Monks carve the great painted caves of Ajanta
events.note: Buddhist murals cover the walls of the rock-cut halls.

events.title: Stamford Raffles founds modern Singapore
events.note: He signed a treaty with the local sultan.

events.title: A tiger hunter stumbles on India's Ajanta Caves
events.note: Officer John Smith scratched his name on a wall inside.

events.title: Future Queen Victoria is born
events.note: Born at Kensington Palace, she reigned for 63 years.

events.title: Ajanta Caves become a World Heritage Site
events.note: UNESCO listed them alongside nearby Ellora.

fact: Sweden's Vasa sank in 1628 and was raised in 1961 — but England's older Mary Rose, sunk in 1545, wasn't raised until 1982.

events.title: England's warship Mary Rose sinks off Portsmouth
events.note: She went down while leading an attack on a French invasion fleet.

events.title: Sweden's warship Vasa sinks on its maiden voyage
events.note: She capsized after sailing only about 1,300 metres.

events.title: Dutch tulip bulb prices collapse
events.note: Single bulbs had sold for more than ten times a craftsman's yearly pay.

events.title: The wreck of the Vasa is lifted from Stockholm harbour
events.note: Her hull came up largely intact after 333 years on the seabed.

events.title: The Mary Rose is raised from the Solent
events.note: The wreck had been located in 1971.

fact: Marie Antoinette was born the day after the great Lisbon earthquake — and Mozart less than three months later.

events.title: An earthquake and tsunami destroy Lisbon
events.note: It struck on All Saints' Day, as churches were full.

events.title: Marie Antoinette is born in Vienna
events.note: She was the 15th child of Empress Maria Theresa.

events.title: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart is born
events.note: Born in Salzburg, the son of a court musician.

events.title: Louis XVI is guillotined
events.note: He was executed in Paris's Place de la Révolution.

events.title: Marie Antoinette is guillotined
events.note: She was executed nine months after her husband.

fact: Saigō Takamori, Japan's 'last samurai', died at Shiroyama 15 months after Custer fell at Little Bighorn.

events.title: Custer is killed at the Little Bighorn
events.note: Lakota and Cheyenne warriors wiped out his command.

events.title: Victoria is proclaimed Empress of India
events.note: The proclamation was read at a vast durbar in Delhi.

events.title: Swan Lake premieres in Moscow
events.note: Tchaikovsky's ballet was poorly received at first.

events.title: Samurai rebels make a last stand at Shiroyama
events.note: Saigō Takamori died as the Satsuma Rebellion ended.

events.title: Edison is granted a patent for the phonograph
events.note: It recorded sound on tinfoil wrapped round a cylinder.

fact: Alexander Selkirk was rescued after four years marooned in 1709; a decade later, Robinson Crusoe was published.

events.title: Peter the Great founds St Petersburg
events.note: He built it on marshland seized from Sweden.

events.title: Marlborough wins the Battle of Blenheim
events.note: The victory later gave its name to Blenheim Palace.

events.title: Castaway Alexander Selkirk is rescued
events.note: He had been marooned on an island off Chile.

events.title: Defoe's Robinson Crusoe is published
events.note: It was presented as a true memoir.

events.title: Swift's Gulliver's Travels is published
events.note: Swift arranged its publication anonymously.

fact: The first big chlorine gas attack, overseen by chemist Fritz Haber, came three days before the Gallipoli landings.

events.title: Fritz Haber makes ammonia from the air
events.note: His process now feeds billions through fertiliser.

events.title: German troops release chlorine gas at Ypres
events.note: A green-yellow cloud drifted onto French colonial troops.

events.title: Allied troops land at Gallipoli
events.note: Anzac Day marks the landings.

events.title: A U-boat sinks the Lusitania
events.note: Nearly 1,200 people died off the coast of Ireland.

events.title: Fritz Haber wins the Nobel Prize in Chemistry
events.note: The award for ammonia synthesis outraged many scientists.

fact: Steller's sea cow was hunted to extinction within 27 years of Europeans discovering it in 1741.

events.title: Vitus Bering's crew discovers Steller's sea cow
events.note: The giant sea cow grew up to 9 m long.

events.title: Jacobites are crushed at the Battle of Culloden
events.note: The last pitched battle fought on British soil.

events.title: Catherine the Great seizes the Russian throne
events.note: She overthrew her own husband, Peter III, in a coup.

events.title: Steller's sea cow is hunted to extinction
events.note: Fur hunters killed the slow animals for meat.

events.title: Captain Cook's Endeavour sails from Plymouth
events.note: On Cook's first great voyage, to observe the transit of Venus.

fact: Brunei only became fully independent from Britain on 1 January 1984 — 23 days before the Apple Macintosh launched.

events.title: Brunei becomes a British protectorate
events.note: Britain took over its foreign affairs.

events.title: Oil is struck at Seria in Brunei
events.note: Oil later made Brunei one of the world's richest nations.

events.title: Brunei becomes independent
events.note: Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah became prime minister too.

events.title: Apple launches the Macintosh
events.note: It was teased in a famous Super Bowl advert.

events.title: Britain hands Hong Kong back to China
events.note: The handover ended 156 years of British rule.

fact: The Chicago Cubs went 108 years between World Series wins — from October 1908, the year of the Tunguska blast, to November 2016.

events.title: The Tunguska explosion flattens a Siberian forest
events.note: An exploding space rock flattened about 80 million trees.

events.title: The Chicago Cubs win the World Series
events.note: They beat the Detroit Tigers for a second straight title.

events.title: Wrigley Field hosts its first game
events.note: It was built for the Chicago Whales of the Federal League.

events.title: The Cubs finally win the World Series again
events.note: They beat Cleveland in extra innings of Game 7.

events.title: Donald Trump is elected US president
events.note: He lost the popular vote but won the Electoral College.

fact: Packaged toilet paper (1857) is closer in time to the iPhone than to Harington's flush toilet design of 1596.

events.title: Sir John Harington describes his flush toilet
events.note: He built one at his house at Kelston, near Bath.

events.title: The Great Exhibition opens in London
events.note: Visitors paid a penny to use its public flushing toilets.

events.title: Joseph Gayetty sells packaged toilet paper
events.note: His 'Medicated Paper' was sold in flat sheets.

events.title: The 'Great Stink' engulfs London
events.note: Hot weather turned the sewage-filled Thames rank.

events.title: The iPhone goes on sale
events.note: Steve Jobs had unveiled it in January.

fact: Within 20 years, Arab armies fought the Franks at Tours (732) and Tang China at Talas (751).

events.title: The Dome of the Rock is completed in Jerusalem
events.note: The oldest surviving major work of Islamic architecture.

events.title: The Franks defeat an Arab army near Tours
events.note: Charles Martel's victory halted the Umayyad advance into France.

events.title: Abbasid and Tang armies clash at Talas
events.note: Legend says captured Chinese brought papermaking west.

events.title: The city of Baghdad is founded
events.note: Built as a perfectly round city on the Tigris.

events.title: Work begins on the Great Mosque of Córdoba
events.note: Its forest of striped arches later enclosed a cathedral.

fact: Indonesia and Vietnam declared independence just 16 days apart in 1945 — Ho Chi Minh's speech quoted America's Declaration.

events.title: Borobudur is brought to the world's attention
events.note: Raffles sent engineer H. C. Cornelius to clear the buried Buddhist temple.

events.title: Ho Chi Minh is born
events.note: Born Nguyễn Sinh Cung in Nghệ An province, then part of French Indochina.

events.title: Sukarno proclaims Indonesia's independence
events.note: Read out in Jakarta two days after Japan announced its surrender.

events.title: Ho Chi Minh declares Vietnam's independence
events.note: He read it to a vast crowd in Hanoi's Ba Đình Square.

events.title: The French garrison at Dien Bien Phu falls
events.note: The defeat ended France's war in Indochina.

fact: Brazil's capital, Brasília, is younger than the microchip: Kilby's first chip worked in 1958, Brasília opened in 1960.

events.title: Rio de Janeiro becomes the capital of Brazil
events.note: The colonial capital moved south from Salvador.

events.title: Christ the Redeemer statue is inaugurated
events.note: It stands 30 metres tall on Corcovado mountain.

events.title: Brazil wins its first World Cup
events.note: A 17-year-old Pelé scored twice in the final against Sweden.

events.title: Jack Kilby demonstrates the integrated circuit
events.note: His first chip, at Texas Instruments, was on a sliver of germanium.

events.title: Brasília is inaugurated as Brazil's capital
events.note: The planned city was built from scratch in about 41 months.

fact: Neil Armstrong died just 19 days after NASA's Curiosity rover landed on Mars.

events.title: Neil Armstrong is born
events.note: Born in Wapakoneta, Ohio.

events.title: London's Shard skyscraper is inaugurated
events.note: It was then the tallest building in the European Union.

events.title: London opens its third Summer Olympics
events.note: Danny Boyle directed the opening ceremony.

events.title: NASA's Curiosity rover lands on Mars
events.note: A rocket-powered 'sky crane' lowered it into Gale Crater.

events.title: Neil Armstrong dies
events.note: He died in Cincinnati after heart surgery, aged 82.

fact: An Englishman, William Adams, reached Japan six months before Sekigahara — the victor, Ieyasu, later made him a samurai.

events.title: English fleet defeats the Armada at Gravelines
events.note: Fireships broke up the Spanish formation the night before.

events.title: Giordano Bruno is burned at the stake in Rome
events.note: He had argued the stars were distant suns.

events.title: English pilot William Adams reaches Japan
events.note: His Dutch ship Liefde limped into Kyushu with a dying crew.

events.title: Tokugawa Ieyasu wins the Battle of Sekigahara
events.note: The victory paved the way for 250 years of Tokugawa rule.

events.title: Twelfth Night is performed at Middle Temple Hall
events.note: A law student’s diary records the performance.

fact: Bram Stoker's Dracula was published less than a month before Queen Victoria's Diamond Jubilee.

events.title: Sherlock Holmes appears in A Study in Scarlet
events.note: Conan Doyle sold it to Beeton's Christmas Annual.

events.title: Bram Stoker's Dracula is published
events.note: Stoker never saw Transylvania.

events.title: London celebrates a queen's Diamond Jubilee
events.note: Queen Victoria marked 60 years on the throne.

events.title: A ship lands a 'ton of gold' in Seattle
events.note: The news set off the Klondike Gold Rush.

events.title: Bram Stoker dies in London
events.note: His obituaries barely mentioned Dracula.

fact: The eclipse photos that proved Einstein right were taken a month before the Treaty of Versailles was signed.

events.title: Einstein presents his field equations of gravity
events.note: He read them to the Prussian Academy in Berlin.

events.title: Eddington photographs a total solar eclipse
events.note: He observed from Príncipe, off West Africa.

events.title: Alcock and Brown land after a nonstop Atlantic flight
events.note: They crash-landed in a bog in Ireland.

events.title: The Treaty of Versailles is signed
events.note: It was signed in the Hall of Mirrors.

events.title: Eclipse results backing relativity are announced
events.note: Einstein woke up world-famous the next day.

fact: The Maya calendar cycle that 'ended' on 21 December 2012 had begun in 3114 BC.

events.title: The Maya calendar's current era begins
events.note: The Long Count reckons days from this mythical creation date.

events.title: The oldest known Long Count date is carved
events.note: It is on a stela at Chiapa de Corzo, Mexico.

events.title: Bishop Landa burns Maya books at Maní
events.note: Only a handful of Maya codices survive today.

events.title: Psy releases 'Gangnam Style'
events.note: It became YouTube's first video to pass a billion views.

events.title: A Maya calendar cycle ends — and the world doesn't
events.note: Doomsday rumours had spread worldwide.

fact: The oldest surviving play, Aeschylus's The Persians (472 BC), is about a real sea battle fought just eight years earlier.

events.title: Greek ships defeat Persia's navy at Salamis
events.note: Themistocles lured the bigger Persian fleet into a narrow strait.

events.title: Aeschylus's play The Persians is first staged
events.note: It was performed in Athens, with the young Pericles as its sponsor.

events.title: A deadly plague breaks out in besieged Athens
events.note: It struck during the Peloponnesian War and later killed Pericles.

events.title: Greece launches its war of independence
events.note: Greeks rose against nearly four centuries of Ottoman rule.

events.title: Michael Ventris deciphers the Linear B script
events.note: It turned out to be an early form of Greek.

fact: Jeanne Calment said she met Van Gogh in Arles as a teenager — and she lived until 1997, after Dolly the sheep was cloned.

events.title: Jeanne Calment is born in Arles
events.note: She would become the oldest person ever verified.

events.title: Van Gogh cuts off his ear in Arles
events.note: It followed a quarrel with fellow painter Paul Gauguin.

events.title: Dolly the sheep is born
events.note: She was the first mammal cloned from an adult cell.

events.title: Tony Blair becomes prime minister
events.note: At 43 he was the youngest British PM since 1812.

events.title: Jeanne Calment dies
events.note: She was 122 years and 164 days old.

fact: The Treaty of Waitangi was signed in New Zealand just four days before Queen Victoria married Prince Albert.

events.title: Opium War's opening clash erupts off Kowloon
events.note: British ships fired on Chinese war junks.

events.title: The Treaty of Waitangi is signed
events.note: British officials and Māori chiefs signed it in the Bay of Islands.

events.title: Queen Victoria marries Prince Albert
events.note: Her white wedding dress set a lasting fashion.

events.title: Claude Monet is born in Paris
events.note: His painting Impression, Sunrise gave Impressionism its name.

events.title: British forces occupy Hong Kong Island
events.note: The Union Jack was raised at Possession Point.

fact: Stravinsky's Rite of Spring sparked uproar in Paris six days before Emily Davison ran onto the Derby course.

events.title: Igor Stravinsky is born
events.note: He was born near St Petersburg.

events.title: The Rite of Spring causes uproar in Paris
events.note: The ballet's premiere sent the audience into a near-riot.

events.title: Suffragette Emily Davison is struck at the Derby
events.note: She ran in front of the King's horse and died days later.

events.title: Niels Bohr publishes his model of the atom
events.note: Electrons in his model orbit the nucleus at fixed levels.

events.title: The US Federal Reserve is created
events.note: Woodrow Wilson signed the Federal Reserve Act.

fact: Joseph Lister first used antiseptic in surgery on 12 Aug 1865 — the day before handwashing pioneer Semmelweis died.

events.title: Semmelweis orders doctors to wash their hands
events.note: Deaths from childbed fever in his Vienna ward plunged.

events.title: Mendel presents his pea-plant experiments
events.note: Hardly anyone noticed his laws of heredity for 35 years.

events.title: Edward Whymper's party conquers the Matterhorn
events.note: Four of the seven climbers died on the descent.

events.title: Joseph Lister treats a wound with carbolic acid
events.note: His patient was an 11-year-old boy with a broken leg.

events.title: Ignaz Semmelweis dies in an asylum
events.note: He was beaten by guards and died of an infected wound.

fact: Cuneiform was written for over 3,000 years — from Uruk around 3300 BC to a last known tablet around AD 75.

events.title: Scribes in Uruk begin writing on clay tablets
events.note: Early tablets mostly tallied grain, beer and livestock.

events.title: Sargon of Akkad builds an empire
events.note: He united the city-states of Mesopotamia.

events.title: The Behistun Inscription is carved on a cliff
events.note: The same text appears in three languages.

events.title: The last known cuneiform tablet is written
events.note: It is an astronomical almanac from Babylonia.

events.title: Four scholars prove cuneiform can be read
events.note: Separate translations of one text came out nearly the same.

fact: Christiaan Huygens discovered Saturn's moon Titan in 1655 — 350 years later, a probe named after him landed on it.

events.title: Christiaan Huygens discovers Saturn's moon Titan
events.note: It was the first moon of Saturn anyone had found.

events.title: Rembrandt dies in Amsterdam
events.note: He was buried in a rented grave in the Westerkerk.

events.title: Holst's The Planets is first performed
events.note: Adrian Boult conducted it for an invited audience in London.

events.title: A huge tsunami strikes around the Indian Ocean
events.note: It was set off by a magnitude 9.2–9.3 earthquake off Sumatra.

events.title: The Huygens probe lands on Saturn's moon Titan
events.note: It is still the only landing ever made in the outer Solar System.

fact: Bonnie and Clyde and John Dillinger were gunned down by lawmen just two months apart, in 1934.

events.title: The Empire State Building opens
events.note: It was the world's tallest building for nearly 40 years.

events.title: Bonnie and Clyde are killed in an ambush
events.note: Officers fired about 130 rounds into their car in Louisiana.

events.title: John Dillinger is shot outside a Chicago cinema
events.note: FBI agents were tipped off by the "Lady in Red".

events.title: Alcatraz receives its first federal inmates
events.note: The island in San Francisco Bay held Al Capone.

events.title: The "Black Sunday" dust storm sweeps the Plains
events.note: It gave the Dust Bowl its name.

fact: Fidel Castro's rebels took Cuba on 1 January 1959 — two days before Alaska became the 49th US state.

events.title: Fidel Castro is born
events.note: He was born on his father's farm in eastern Cuba.

events.title: Batista flees as Castro's revolution wins
events.note: The dictator left Havana in the early hours of New Year's Day.

events.title: Alaska becomes a US state
events.note: It is the largest state by area.

events.title: Buddy Holly dies in a plane crash
events.note: It became known as 'The Day the Music Died'.

events.title: Hawaii becomes a US state
events.note: It was the 50th and most recent state.

fact: Charlotte Cooper became the first woman Olympic champion on 11 July 1900 — eight days before the Paris Métro opened.

events.title: The Paris Exposition Universelle opens
events.note: The Olympic Games were held as a sideshow to the fair.

events.title: The Siege of the International Legations begins
events.note: Boxer rebels besieged foreign diplomats in Beijing for 55 days.

events.title: The Zeppelin airship makes its maiden flight
events.note: LZ 1 flew over Lake Constance for about 18 minutes.

events.title: Charlotte Cooper wins Olympic tennis gold
events.note: The British player won the women's singles in Paris.

events.title: The Paris Métro opens
events.note: Line 1 ran from Porte de Vincennes to Porte Maillot.

fact: A voice was recorded in Paris in April 1860 — before Lincoln was elected, and nearly 18 years before Edison's phonograph patent.

events.title: The Pony Express begins carrying mail
events.note: Riders crossed from Missouri to California in about ten days.

events.title: Édouard-Léon Scott records 'Au clair de la lune'
events.note: His phonautograph traced sound but could not play it back.

events.title: Abraham Lincoln is elected president
events.note: He won without carrying a single Southern state.

events.title: Edison patents the phonograph
events.note: It recorded on tinfoil wrapped around a cylinder.

events.title: Emile Berliner patents the gramophone
events.note: Flat discs replaced Edison's cylinders.

fact: 'Kamikaze' means divine wind — the typhoon that wrecked Kublai Khan's fleet off Japan in 1281, while Marco Polo served him.

events.title: Kublai Khan proclaims the Yuan dynasty
events.note: He took a Chinese dynastic name for his Mongol realm.

events.title: Marco Polo reaches Kublai Khan's court
events.note: He arrived at Shangdu, the summer capital known as Xanadu.

events.title: A typhoon wrecks the Mongol fleet off Japan
events.note: Japanese called the storm kamikaze, the 'divine wind'.

events.title: Marco Polo returns home to Venice
events.note: He had been away for 24 years.

events.title: Japan flies its first kamikaze attacks
events.note: Suicide pilots struck US ships in the Battle of Leyte Gulf.

fact: Abebe Bikila won the 1960 Olympic marathon barefoot in Rome — 24 years after Italy's army marched into Addis Ababa.

events.title: Haile Selassie is crowned emperor of Ethiopia
events.note: Guests at the Addis Ababa coronation came from across the world.

events.title: Italian troops march into Addis Ababa
events.note: Mussolini's army occupied Ethiopia until 1941.

events.title: Abebe Bikila wins the Olympic marathon barefoot
events.note: He was Ethiopia's first Olympic champion.

events.title: Haile Selassie is deposed by the army
events.note: The Derg military junta took power and ended the monarchy.

events.title: Live Aid raises money for Ethiopia's famine
events.note: Concerts in London and Philadelphia were watched by a vast global audience.

fact: Intel launched its first microprocessor just nine days before D. B. Cooper hijacked a jet and vanished.

events.title: The Boeing jumbo jet enters service
events.note: Pan Am flew it from New York to London.

events.title: Walt Disney World opens in Florida
events.note: Walt himself had died five years earlier.

events.title: Intel launches its first microprocessor
events.note: A whole computer processor on one chip, for a calculator.

events.title: D. B. Cooper parachutes from a hijacked jet
events.note: He jumped with $200,000 in ransom and was never identified.

events.title: Burglars break into the Watergate building
events.note: The break-in led to Nixon's resignation two years later.

fact: The China Syndrome, a film about a nuclear meltdown, opened just 12 days before the Three Mile Island accident.

events.title: Obninsk power plant joins the grid
events.note: The Soviet plant fed electricity into a power grid.

events.title: The China Syndrome opens in cinemas
events.note: Jane Fonda and Jack Lemmon starred.

events.title: Three Mile Island nuclear accident
events.note: A reactor partially melted down in Pennsylvania.

events.title: John Wayne dies
events.note: The Western star had won his only Oscar for True Grit.

events.title: Sony's Walkman goes on sale
events.note: The portable cassette player launched in Japan.

fact: Emperor Nero was crowned winner of an Olympic chariot race in 67 AD though he fell out of his chariot — three years after Rome burned.

events.title: The Great Fire of Rome breaks out
events.note: It burned for six days; rumours blamed Nero.

events.title: Nero competes at the Olympic Games
events.note: He had the Games postponed a year so that he could take part.

events.title: Nero dies by suicide
events.note: His last words reportedly were "What an artist dies in me!"

events.title: Roman troops destroy the Temple in Jerusalem
events.note: The siege was led by Titus, son of the new emperor Vespasian.

events.title: The Colosseum is inaugurated in Rome
events.note: Emperor Titus opened it with 100 days of games.

fact: The QWERTY typewriter went on sale closer in time to the US Constitution's signing than to the first text message.

events.title: The US Constitution is signed
events.note: It was signed at Independence Hall in Philadelphia.

events.title: Stanley meets Livingstone
events.note: The meeting took place at Ujiji on Lake Tanganyika.

events.title: The Sholes and Glidden typewriter goes on sale
events.note: Remington built it with the QWERTY layout still used today.

events.title: A dam bursts above Johnstown, Pennsylvania
events.note: More than 2,200 people died in the flood.

events.title: The first text message is sent
events.note: Neil Papworth texted 'Merry Christmas' to a Vodafone director.

fact: Ibn Battuta left Tangier in 1325 on pilgrimage to Mecca and didn't come home for 24 years — he got as far as China.

events.title: Sundiata defeats the Sosso at Kirina
events.note: The victory founded the Mali Empire.

events.title: Ibn Battuta sets out from Tangier
events.note: He was 21 and bound for Mecca.

events.title: Djinguereber Mosque is built in Timbuktu
events.note: Its mud-brick walls are still replastered by hand.

events.title: Ibn Battuta returns home to Morocco
events.note: His mother had died a few months before he arrived.

events.title: Timbuktu is named a World Heritage Site
events.note: Its mosques and manuscripts recall a great centre of learning.

fact: Pelé scored his 1,000th goal five days after Apollo 12 launched — on the very day it landed on the Moon.

events.title: Santos-Dumont flies his 14-bis plane in Paris
events.note: The Brazilian won a prize for flying over 25 metres.

events.title: Uruguay stuns Brazil in the Maracanã World Cup decider
events.note: Brazilians still call the defeat the Maracanazo.

events.title: Apollo 12 is struck by lightning as it launches
events.note: The crew restored power and carried on to the Moon.

events.title: Pelé scores his thousandth goal
events.note: A penalty for Santos against Vasco da Gama at the Maracanã.

events.title: Ayrton Senna is killed at Imola
events.note: The three-time Brazilian world champion crashed in the San Marino Grand Prix.

fact: Ole Rømer showed in 1676 that light travels at a finite speed — 22 years before Thomas Savery patented his steam pump.

events.title: Molière collapses on stage and dies
events.note: He was playing the lead in his own The Imaginary Invalid.

events.title: Ole Rømer shows that light has a finite speed
events.note: He timed the eclipses of Jupiter's moon Io.

events.title: Pueblo peoples rise up against Spanish rule
events.note: They drove the Spanish out of Santa Fe for twelve years.

events.title: Thomas Savery patents a steam-powered pump
events.note: It was meant to pump water out of mines.

events.title: Thomas Newcomen's steam engine goes to work
events.note: It pumped water from a coal mine near Dudley.

fact: Edgar Allan Poe and Frédéric Chopin died just ten days apart, in October 1849.

events.title: Mormon pioneers reach the Salt Lake Valley
events.note: Utah still marks the day as a state holiday, Pioneer Day.

events.title: The Communist Manifesto is published
events.note: Marx and Engels wrote it in German; it appeared in London.

events.title: Walter Hunt patents the safety pin
events.note: He sold the rights for a few hundred dollars.

events.title: Edgar Allan Poe dies in Baltimore
events.note: He had been found delirious in the street days earlier.

events.title: Frédéric Chopin dies in Paris
events.note: His heart was taken back to Warsaw.

fact: Brazil abolished slavery in May 1888 — and its emperor was overthrown 18 months later.

events.title: Brazil abolishes slavery with the Golden Law
events.note: It was the last country in the Americas to do so.

events.title: Van Gogh cuts off part of his ear
events.note: It followed a quarrel with Gauguin in Arles.

events.title: Nellie Bly sets off to circle the globe
events.note: She made it in 72 days, beating Phileas Fogg's 80.

events.title: Brazil's emperor is overthrown
events.note: Pedro II was sent into exile in Europe.

events.title: Nellie Bly arrives home after circling the globe
events.note: She beat Phileas Fogg’s fictional 80 days, taking just over 72.

fact: Dr. No, the first Bond film, opened 11 days before the Cuban Missile Crisis — the same day as the Beatles' first single.

events.title: Ian Fleming's Casino Royale is published
events.note: The novel introduced James Bond.

events.title: Marilyn Monroe dies
events.note: She was found at her home in Los Angeles.

events.title: Dr. No premieres in London
events.note: Sean Connery played Bond for the first time.

events.title: The Cuban Missile Crisis begins
events.note: Kennedy was shown spy-plane photos of Soviet missiles.

events.title: The Beatles release Please Please Me
events.note: The album was recorded in about ten hours.

fact: Fibonacci popularised Hindu–Arabic numerals in Europe in 1202 — four years before Genghis Khan was proclaimed.

events.title: The foundation stone of Notre-Dame de Paris is laid
events.note: The cathedral took nearly two centuries to finish.

events.title: Fibonacci publishes Liber Abaci
events.note: It taught merchants to calculate with digits 0 to 9.

events.title: Crusaders sack Constantinople
events.note: The Fourth Crusade turned on a Christian city.

events.title: Temüjin is proclaimed Genghis Khan
events.note: A great assembly by the Onon River named him ruler.

events.title: The University of Cambridge is founded
events.note: Scholars fleeing a dispute in Oxford set it up.

fact: Alexander the Great founded Alexandria in Egypt in 331 BC — and five years later he was fighting in India.

events.title: Philip II of Macedon is assassinated
events.note: A bodyguard stabbed him at his daughter's wedding.

events.title: Alexander founds Alexandria in Egypt
events.note: It grew into the largest city of the Mediterranean.

events.title: Alexander defeats King Porus at the Hydaspes
events.note: Porus fielded war elephants against the Macedonians.

events.title: Alexander the Great dies in Babylon
events.note: He was 32; the cause is still debated.

events.title: Euclid writes the Elements
events.note: He worked in Alexandria.

fact: Siena's Monte dei Paschi bank was founded in 1472 — 22 years before Luca Pacioli first set out double-entry bookkeeping in print.

events.title: The Medici Bank is founded in Florence
events.note: It became the largest and most respected bank in Europe.

events.title: Gutenberg finishes printing his Bible
events.note: About 180 copies were printed in Mainz.

events.title: Monte dei Paschi bank is founded in Siena
events.note: It is often called the oldest bank still in business.

events.title: Luca Pacioli publishes the rules of double-entry bookkeeping
events.note: They appeared in his maths textbook, the Summa, printed in Venice.

events.title: Savonarola's followers light the Bonfire of the Vanities
events.note: Mirrors, books and paintings were burned in Florence.

fact: Queen Victoria and poet Walt Whitman were born just a week apart, in May 1819.

events.title: The steamship Savannah sets out across the Atlantic
events.note: It was the first steamship to cross the Atlantic, though mostly under sail.

events.title: Future Queen Victoria is born
events.note: Born at Kensington Palace in London.

events.title: Walt Whitman is born
events.note: Born on Long Island, New York; he later wrote Leaves of Grass.

events.title: Alabama becomes a US state
events.note: It was the 22nd state admitted to the Union.

events.title: Queen Victoria dies
events.note: She died on the Isle of Wight after reigning for 63 years.

fact: Persia's Nader Shah sacked Delhi less than a month before highwayman Dick Turpin was hanged in York.

events.title: Gulliver's Travels is published
events.note: Jonathan Swift's satire sold out within a week.

events.title: John Wesley feels his heart 'strangely warmed'
events.note: His Aldersgate Street conversion launched the Methodist revival.

events.title: Persian troops sack Delhi
events.note: Nader Shah carried off the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor.

events.title: Dick Turpin is hanged in York
events.note: The highwayman had been caught for horse theft.

events.title: Vitus Bering dies on a remote island
events.note: His crew was shipwrecked on what is now Bering Island.

fact: The Simpsons debuted as a half-hour series less than six weeks after the Berlin Wall fell.

events.title: The Exxon Valdez spills oil off Alaska
events.note: Some 11 million US gallons of crude oil leaked.

events.title: The Berlin Wall falls
events.note: Crowds crossed after a botched announcement.

events.title: The Simpsons premieres as a series
events.note: The first episode was a Christmas special.

events.title: Romania's Ceaușescu is executed after a show trial
events.note: He and his wife Elena were shot by firing squad.

events.title: Nelson Mandela walks free from prison
events.note: He had been imprisoned for 27 years.

fact: Tycho Brahe's 'new star' lit up the sky in Nov 1572 — less than three months after the St. Bartholomew's Day massacre.

events.title: The Battle of Lepanto
events.note: A Holy League fleet crushed the Ottoman navy.

events.title: The St. Bartholomew's Day massacre begins
events.note: Catholic mobs killed thousands of Huguenots in Paris.

events.title: Tycho Brahe spots a 'new star' in Cassiopeia
events.note: The supernova showed the heavens could change.

events.title: Kepler's supernova appears
events.note: It is the last supernova seen in our galaxy with the naked eye.

events.title: The Gunpowder Plot is foiled
events.note: Guy Fawkes was caught guarding barrels under Parliament.

fact: Britain only became an island around 6500 BC — well over a thousand years after Cheddar Man died.

events.title: Cheddar Man dies young in what is now Somerset
events.note: He is Britain's oldest near-complete human skeleton.

events.title: Rising seas cut Britain off from Europe
events.note: The lost land under the North Sea is called Doggerland.

events.title: Cheddar Man is found in Gough's Cave
events.note: Workers found him while improving drainage.

events.title: The Channel Tunnel opens
events.note: Queen Elizabeth II and President Mitterrand opened it.

events.title: DNA shows Cheddar Man had dark skin
events.note: He probably also had blue eyes.

fact: China scrapped its 1,300-year-old imperial exams just three days before Russia and Japan signed the Treaty of Portsmouth.

events.title: Lin Zexu destroys British opium at Humen
events.note: Over 1,000 tonnes were mixed with lime and salt and flushed out to sea.

events.title: Japan's navy destroys Russia's fleet at Tsushima
events.note: Admiral Tōgō sank or captured most of the Russian Baltic Fleet.

events.title: China abolishes its imperial civil-service exams
events.note: The exams had chosen officials since the Sui dynasty.

events.title: The Treaty of Portsmouth ends the Russo-Japanese War
events.note: Theodore Roosevelt won the Nobel Peace Prize for brokering it.

events.title: China's gaokao university exam is held again
events.note: It had been suspended for over a decade by the Cultural Revolution.

fact: The Pyrenean ibex died out in January 2000 — then a cloned kid was born in 2003 and lived for a few minutes.

events.title: Dolly the sheep is born
events.note: The first mammal cloned from an adult cell.

events.title: The last Pyrenean ibex dies in Spain
events.note: A falling tree killed Celia, the last of the bucardo.

events.title: Wikipedia goes online
events.note: Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger launched it.

events.title: A cloned Pyrenean ibex is born
events.note: Cloned from Celia's cells, it died minutes after birth.

events.title: Concorde makes its final commercial flight
events.note: It flew from New York to London Heathrow.

fact: Sally Ride became the first American woman in space 20 years and two days after Valentina Tereshkova flew.

events.title: Sally Ride is born
events.note: She was born in Los Angeles.

events.title: Valentina Tereshkova flies into space
events.note: She orbited Earth 48 times aboard Vostok 6.

events.title: Return of the Jedi opens in cinemas
events.note: It completed the original Star Wars trilogy.

events.title: Sally Ride flies on the Space Shuttle
events.note: She flew on Challenger's STS-7 mission.

events.title: Space Shuttle Challenger breaks apart
events.note: It broke up 73 seconds after liftoff.

fact: Constantinople's Hagia Sophia was rebuilt because of sports fans: chariot-racing factions burned the old church in the Nika riots.

events.title: Justinian's law code is first published
events.note: It still underpins civil law across much of Europe.

events.title: Chariot-racing fans start the Nika riots
events.note: Blues and Greens united against Justinian; about 30,000 died.

events.title: The domed Hagia Sophia is dedicated
events.note: It was the world's largest cathedral for nearly a thousand years.

events.title: The Plague of Justinian reaches Constantinople
events.note: At its peak it reportedly killed thousands a day in the city.

events.title: Emperor Justinian dies in Constantinople
events.note: He had ruled the Eastern Roman Empire for 38 years.

fact: The world's first cash machine opened in London two days after the Beatles sang All You Need Is Love to a global audience.

events.title: Diners Club launches its charge card
events.note: It began after Frank McNamara forgot his wallet at dinner.

events.title: Israel launches the Six-Day War
events.note: Israel took Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank and the Golan Heights.

events.title: The Beatles sing on the Our World broadcast
events.note: An estimated 400 million or more people watched live.

events.title: The first ATM opens in London
events.note: Barclays' cash machine in Enfield used paper vouchers.

events.title: The first human heart transplant
events.note: Christiaan Barnard operated in Cape Town.

fact: Rounded up on Friday 13 October 1307, the Knights Templar had existed for less than 200 years.

events.title: The Knights Templar are founded in Jerusalem
events.note: Nine knights vowed to protect pilgrims to the Holy Land.

events.title: Acre falls, ending the crusader kingdom
events.note: The Mamluks took the last major crusader city.

events.title: France arrests the Knights Templar
events.note: The dawn raids fell on a Friday the 13th.

events.title: Jacques de Molay is burned at the stake
events.note: The last Grand Master died on an island in the Seine.

events.title: The Da Vinci Code is published
events.note: Dan Brown's thriller wove in Templar legends.

fact: Siam ended absolute monarchy on 24 June 1932 — and on the same date in 1939, it renamed itself Thailand.

events.title: Chang and Eng, the original 'Siamese twins', are born
events.note: The conjoined brothers later settled in North Carolina.

events.title: A bloodless revolution ends absolute monarchy in Siam
events.note: The People's Party seized Bangkok while the king was at the seaside.

events.title: Siam officially renames itself Thailand
events.note: Prime Minister Plaek Phibunsongkhram pushed the change.

events.title: The Burma 'Death Railway' is completed
events.note: Built for Japan by prisoners of war and Asian labourers.

events.title: The King and I opens on Broadway
events.note: Rodgers and Hammerstein's musical about a governess at Siam's court.

fact: After Trieste reached the ocean's deepest point in 1960, nobody went back for 52 years — until James Cameron in 2012.

events.title: Beebe and Barton dive half a mile in a bathysphere
events.note: They reached 923 m off Bermuda in a steel sphere.

events.title: Trieste reaches the bottom of the Challenger Deep
events.note: Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh spent 20 minutes at the bottom.

events.title: The wreck of the Titanic is found
events.note: Robert Ballard's team found it at a depth of 3.8 km.

events.title: James Cameron dives solo to the Challenger Deep
events.note: The Titanic director piloted the Deepsea Challenger.

events.title: Felix Baumgartner skydives from the stratosphere
events.note: He broke the sound barrier in free fall over New Mexico.

fact: Germany brought in daylight saving time in April 1916 to save coal for the war; Britain copied it three weeks later.

events.title: The Battle of Verdun begins
events.note: It became the longest battle of the war.

events.title: The Easter Rising begins in Dublin
events.note: Irish rebels seized the General Post Office.

events.title: Germany puts its clocks forward
events.note: It was the first nationwide daylight saving time.

events.title: Britain adopts British Summer Time
events.note: William Willett had campaigned for it for years.

events.title: The Battle of the Somme begins
events.note: Britain suffered about 57,000 casualties on the first day.

fact: Mexico City's Tlatelolco massacre happened just ten days before the 1968 Olympics opened there.

events.title: Martin Luther King Jr. is assassinated
events.note: He was shot on a motel balcony in Memphis.

events.title: Troops fire on protesters at Tlatelolco
events.note: Hundreds of students may have been killed in Mexico City.

fact: In the 1667 Treaty of Breda the Dutch kept Run, a tiny nutmeg island, and let England keep Manhattan.

events.title: Pocahontas marries John Rolfe in Virginia
events.note: The marriage brought a brief peace with the Powhatan people.

events.title: Peter Minuit buys Manhattan from the Lenape
events.note: The famous price was 60 guilders' worth of goods.

events.title: The English seize New Amsterdam
events.note: It was renamed New York after the Duke of York.

events.title: The Great Plague sweeps London
events.note: It killed perhaps a quarter of the city’s people.

events.title: The Treaty of Breda is signed
events.note: It ended the Second Anglo-Dutch War.

fact: Big Ben first rang out in July 1859, less than seven weeks before Edwin Drake struck oil in Pennsylvania.

events.title: Blondin crosses Niagara Falls on a tightrope
events.note: He later crossed blindfolded and on stilts.

events.title: Big Ben first chimes at Westminster
events.note: The great bell cracked that September.

events.title: Drake strikes oil in Titusville
events.note: It sparked America's first oil boom.

events.title: John Brown raids Harpers Ferry

events.title: Rockefeller founds Standard Oil

fact: The Sutton Hoo ship burial was dug up in the summer of 1939 — weeks before Britain went to war with Germany.

events.title: Bede completes his history of the English church

events.title: Diggers uncover the Sutton Hoo ship burial
events.note: Self-taught archaeologist Basil Brown led the dig.

events.title: Britain declares war on Germany

events.title: A metal detectorist finds the Staffordshire Hoard
events.note: The largest hoard of Anglo-Saxon gold ever found.

fact: Iran's Shah threw a lavish party at Persepolis in 1971 for 2,500 years of monarchy — and fled into exile seven years later.

events.title: Alexander's army burns Persepolis

events.title: Persia asks the world to call it Iran
events.note: Reza Shah wanted foreign governments to use the country's own name.

events.title: The Shah throws a party at Persepolis for the monarchy

events.title: The Shah leaves Iran for exile
events.note: Mohammad Reza Pahlavi never returned.

events.title: Ayatollah Khomeini returns to Tehran
events.note: Millions greeted his flight from Paris after 14 years in exile.

fact: Kon-Tiki was still adrift on its balsa raft in the mid-Pacific when the Roswell "flying disc" story broke in July 1947.

events.title: Edwin Land demonstrates the instant camera
events.note: Polaroid pictures developed in about a minute.

events.title: The Kon-Tiki raft sets off from Peru
events.note: Thor Heyerdahl wanted to show Polynesia could be reached by raft.

events.title: The Roswell "flying disc" is announced
events.note: The army later said it was a weather balloon.

events.title: Kon-Tiki crashes onto a Polynesian reef
events.note: It ended 101 days and about 6,900 km later at Raroia.

events.title: Chuck Yeager breaks the sound barrier
events.note: He flew the Bell X-1 rocket plane over California.

fact: Angola won independence from Portugal just nine days before Spain's dictator Franco died, in November 1975.

events.title: António Salazar becomes Portugal's leader
events.note: He ruled Portugal for over 35 years.

events.title: Portugal's Carnation Revolution
events.note: Soldiers overthrew the dictatorship almost without bloodshed.

events.title: Queen release 'Bohemian Rhapsody'
events.note: The six-minute single topped the UK chart for nine weeks.

events.title: Angola becomes independent
events.note: Civil war broke out almost at once.

events.title: Francisco Franco dies
events.note: Spain then moved toward democracy under King Juan Carlos.

fact: When Guinness World Records was first published in 1955, Arthur Guinness's 9,000-year brewery lease still had over 8,800 years to run.

events.title: Robert Burns is born in Ayrshire
events.note: Scots still celebrate his birthday with Burns Night suppers.

events.title: Britain wins the Battle of the Plains of Abraham
events.note: Both generals, Wolfe and Montcalm, were killed.

events.title: Arthur Guinness leases St James's Gate brewery
events.note: He agreed to pay £45 a year for 9,000 years.

events.title: The Guinness Book of Records is first published
events.note: It was meant to settle pub arguments.

events.title: James Dean dies in a car crash
events.note: Two of his three starring films were released after his death.

fact: George Orwell died only about seven months after Nineteen Eighty-Four was published.

events.title: Orwell's Animal Farm is published
events.note: Several publishers had turned it down.

events.title: NATO is founded
events.note: Twelve countries signed the treaty in Washington.

events.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four is published
events.note: It gave the world Big Brother and doublethink.

events.title: The Soviet Union tests its first atomic bomb
events.note: The test site was in Kazakhstan.

events.title: George Orwell dies
events.note: He died of tuberculosis in a London hospital.

fact: Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction four months before Darwin set sail on the Beagle.

events.title: Alessandro Volta builds the electric battery
events.note: His 'pile' stacked zinc and copper discs with brine.

events.title: Nat Turner leads a slave rebellion in Virginia
events.note: It was crushed within days; Turner hid for two months.

events.title: Faraday discovers electromagnetic induction
events.note: Moving magnetism made electricity flow in a coil.

events.title: Darwin sets sail on HMS Beagle
events.note: The voyage lasted almost five years.

events.title: Samuel Colt patents his revolver
events.note: He was only 21.

fact: Schliemann's 'Priam's Treasure' came from a city built around 2550 BC — over 1,300 years before the Trojan War of legend.

events.title: The city of Troy II is built
events.note: Schliemann wrongly took this layer for Homer's Troy.

events.title: The Trojan War ends, by Greek reckoning
events.note: Eratosthenes dated the fall of Troy to this year.

events.title: Schliemann uncovers 'Priam's Treasure'
events.note: His wife Sophia was photographed wearing the jewels.

events.title: Heinrich Schliemann dies in Naples
events.note: He collapsed on Christmas Day after visiting Pompeii.

events.title: Moscow admits it holds Priam's Treasure
events.note: The Red Army had taken it from Berlin in 1945.

fact: Germany raised a giant statue of Arminius in 1875 for his AD 9 defeat of Rome — the likely battlefield wasn't found until 1987.

events.title: Germanic tribes wipe out three Roman legions
events.note: The ambush in the Teutoburg Forest was led by Arminius.

events.title: Rome's rebuilt Pantheon is completed
events.note: Its dome is still the largest of unreinforced concrete.

events.title: Emperor Marcus Aurelius dies
events.note: His Meditations are still read today.

events.title: The Hermannsdenkmal statue is unveiled in Germany
events.note: The sword-waving figure of Arminius stands near Detmold.

events.title: A British officer finds Roman coins at Kalkriese
events.note: Major Tony Clunn's finds led to the lost battlefield.

fact: Matilda McCrear, a survivor of the last US slave ship, died in January 1940 — less than a month after Gone with the Wind premiered.

events.title: The Clotilda smuggles captive Africans into Alabama
events.note: It was the last known slave ship to reach the United States.

events.title: Abraham Lincoln is elected president
events.note: He won without carrying a single Southern state.

events.title: Gone with the Wind premieres in Atlanta
events.note: Its Black cast members were barred from the segregated premiere.

events.title: The last known Clotilda survivor dies
events.note: Matilda McCrear had been about two when she was taken.

events.title: Germany invades Denmark and Norway
events.note: Denmark surrendered within hours.

fact: Bangkok became Siam's capital in April 1782 — more than a year before Britain formally recognised US independence.

events.title: Burmese armies sack Ayutthaya
events.note: Siam's capital for over 400 years was burned.

events.title: Goethe publishes The Sorrows of Young Werther
events.note: The novel set off a craze for yellow waistcoats across Europe.

events.title: Bangkok becomes the capital of Siam
events.note: King Rama I moved the court across the Chao Phraya river.

events.title: The Treaty of Paris ends the American Revolution
events.note: Britain recognised the independence of the United States.

events.title: Humans fly in a hot-air balloon
events.note: A Montgolfier balloon carried two men over Paris.

fact: Jules Verne's From the Earth to the Moon launched three men from Florida — 103 years before Apollo 8 did.

events.title: Jules Verne's From the Earth to the Moon is published
events.note: His moon gun was fired from a site in Florida.

events.title: Robert Goddard launches a liquid-fuelled rocket
events.note: It flew for about two seconds in Massachusetts.

events.title: JFK says 'We choose to go to the Moon'
events.note: He spoke at Rice University in Houston.

events.title: Star Trek first airs on US television
events.note: NBC cancelled it after three seasons.

events.title: Apollo 8 launches for the Moon
events.note: Its crew were the first humans to orbit the Moon.

fact: The first image of a black hole was released just five days before Notre-Dame de Paris caught fire.

events.title: Einstein predicts gravitational waves
events.note: He doubted they could ever be detected.

events.title: Scientists announce they have detected gravitational waves
events.note: LIGO caught two black holes merging.

events.title: The first image of a black hole is released
events.note: It showed the glowing ring around M87's black hole.

events.title: Notre-Dame de Paris catches fire
events.note: The cathedral's spire collapsed.

events.title: Game of Thrones airs its final episode
events.note: The ending was widely panned by fans.

fact: Eratosthenes measured the Earth around 240 BC — over 1,700 years before anyone sailed all the way round it.

events.title: Eratosthenes measures the Earth's circumference
events.note: He compared shadows at Syene and Alexandria.

events.title: Magellan sets sail from Spain
events.note: He led five ships and about 270 men.

events.title: Magellan is killed on Mactan
events.note: Lapulapu's warriors defeated his landing party.

events.title: The Victoria returns to Spain after circling the globe
events.note: Only 18 of the original crew made it back.

events.title: Apollo 8 photographs 'Earthrise'
events.note: Bill Anders took the photo from lunar orbit.

fact: Salvator Mundi, painted around 1500 and attributed to Leonardo, sold for a record $450 million in November 2017.

events.title: Leonardo paints Christ as Salvator Mundi
events.note: It was probably commissioned by King Louis XII of France.

events.title: Explorer Amerigo Vespucci dies in Seville
events.note: A German map had already named the New World America after him.

events.title: The Louvre Abu Dhabi opens
events.note: Its huge latticed dome was designed by Jean Nouvel.

events.title: A Leonardo painting sells for a world-record price
events.note: A Saudi prince bought it at Christie's in New York.

events.title: Robert Mugabe resigns as Zimbabwe's president
events.note: He had led the country for 37 years.

fact: Moctezuma died in Tenochtitlan just weeks after Henry VIII met Francis I at the Field of the Cloth of Gold.

events.title: Thomas More publishes Utopia
events.note: The book coined the word for an imagined perfect society.

events.title: Cortés meets Moctezuma in Tenochtitlan
events.note: The Aztec ruler welcomed the Spaniards into his capital.

events.title: Henry VIII meets Francis I at the Cloth of Gold
events.note: Both kings camped in lavish tents near Calais.

events.title: Moctezuma dies
events.note: Accounts differ on whether Spaniards or Aztecs killed him.

events.title: Suleiman the Magnificent becomes sultan
events.note: He ruled the Ottoman Empire for 46 years.

fact: The Ottoman sultan wiped out his Janissary corps just 19 days before Thomas Jefferson died.

events.title: The Ottoman sultan destroys the Janissaries
events.note: Mahmud II's cannon crushed the elite corps' revolt.

events.title: Thomas Jefferson dies at Monticello
events.note: John Adams died the same day, 50 years after the Declaration.

events.title: Beethoven dies in Vienna
events.note: Thousands lined the streets for his funeral.

events.title: Allied fleet destroys an Ottoman navy at Navarino
events.note: It was the last major battle fought wholly with sailing ships.

events.title: Shaka Zulu is assassinated
events.note: His half-brothers Dingane and Mhlangana killed him.

fact: Nadia Comăneci scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics just two days before Viking 1 landed on Mars.

events.title: Concorde starts passenger service
events.note: British Airways and Air France flew the first commercial routes.

events.title: Apple Computer is founded
events.note: Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne started it.

events.title: Californian wines beat French ones in Paris
events.note: Blind tasters at the "Judgment of Paris" picked US wines.

events.title: Nadia Comăneci scores a perfect 10
events.note: The Montreal scoreboard could only show it as 1.00.

events.title: Viking 1 lands on Mars
events.note: It sent back the first photos from the Martian surface.

fact: Peugeot was founded in 1810 — two years before the Brothers Grimm published their fairy tales.

events.title: The US buys Louisiana from France
events.note: It doubled the size of the United States.

events.title: Peugeot is founded as a family business
events.note: It began with a steel foundry that soon made saws and coffee grinders.

events.title: Napoleon's army enters Moscow
events.note: The city was soon set ablaze.

events.title: The Brothers Grimm publish their fairy tales
events.note: The first volume had 86 stories.

events.title: Peugeot applies for its lion trademark
events.note: The lion logo still appears on its cars today.

fact: China and Byzantium each had a woman reign as emperor in her own right — Wu Zetian from 690, Irene from 797.

events.title: Wu Zetian becomes China's empress regnant
events.note: She founded her own Zhou dynasty.

events.title: Japan's Kojiki chronicle is completed
events.note: The oldest surviving book from Japan.

events.title: The An Lushan rebellion begins in China
events.note: The revolt devastated the Tang dynasty.

events.title: Irene becomes sole ruler of Byzantium
events.note: She had her own son blinded to take the throne.

events.title: Vikings sack Paris
events.note: Ragnar's raiders were paid 7,000 pounds of silver to leave.

fact: In December 1999, 11 days apart, Portugal handed Macau to China and the US handed the Panama Canal to Panama.

events.title: Balboa sights the Pacific from Panama

events.title: Portuguese traders settle at Macau
events.note: Ming officials let them stay in return for rent.

events.title: France begins digging a Panama canal

events.title: Portugal hands Macau back to China
events.note: Macau became a special administrative region, like Hong Kong.

events.title: The US hands the Panama Canal to Panama
events.note: Under treaties Jimmy Carter signed with Omar Torrijos in 1977.

fact: Antarctica was first sighted in January 1820 — less than three months before farmers unearthed the Venus de Milo.

events.title: Cavalry charge a crowd at Peterloo, Manchester

events.title: A Russian expedition first sights Antarctica

events.title: The Venus de Milo is unearthed

events.title: Margaret Thatcher leaves office

events.title: The first website goes live at CERN

fact: Gertrude Ederle swam the English Channel in 1926, 51 years after Matthew Webb did it — and nearly two hours faster than any man.

events.title: Matthew Webb swims the English Channel
events.note: He took nearly 22 hours, fuelled by brandy and beef tea.

events.title: Gertrude Ederle swims the English Channel
events.note: The American was the first woman to make the crossing.

events.title: Rudolph Valentino dies
events.note: Huge crowds rioted outside his funeral home in New York.

events.title: Harry Houdini dies

events.title: Iran issues a fatwa against Salman Rushdie

events.title: Tim Berners-Lee proposes the World Wide Web

events.title: The Game Boy goes on sale in Japan

events.title: China crushes the Tiananmen Square protests

events.title: Saladin retakes Jerusalem from the crusaders

events.title: Crusaders sack Constantinople

events.title: French troops carry Venice's bronze horses to Paris

events.title: The US says it will approve the birth-control pill

events.title: Sirimavo Bandaranaike becomes Ceylon's prime minister

events.title: Sri Lanka wins the Cricket World Cup

events.title: Ivan the Terrible is crowned tsar

events.title: King Henry VIII dies

events.title: England's Queen Mary marries Philip of Spain

fact: Wagner's Ring cycle premiered at Bayreuth exactly seven weeks after Custer's Last Stand.

events.title: The Battle of the Nations begins at Leipzig

events.title: Custer's Last Stand at Little Bighorn

events.title: Wild Bill Hickok is shot during a poker game

events.title: The first Bayreuth Festival opens
