fact: Fred Hoyle coined 'Big Bang' on BBC radio in March 1949 to mock the theory — a week before NATO was founded.

events.title: Fred Hoyle coins the term 'Big Bang'

events.title: NATO is founded in Washington
events.note: Twelve countries signed the North Atlantic Treaty.

events.title: George Orwell publishes Nineteen Eighty-Four

events.title: Mao proclaims the People's Republic of China

events.title: Penzias and Wilson detect the Big Bang's afterglow
events.note: They first blamed pigeon droppings for the hiss.

fact: People in Peru were popping corn around 4700 BC; Percy Spencer popped it with microwaves in 1945.

events.title: People in Peru pop corn

events.title: Charles Cretors builds a steam popcorn machine

events.title: Percy Spencer pops corn with microwaves

events.title: Orville Redenbacher's popcorn goes national

events.title: Microwave popcorn bags hit the market

fact: Petrarch climbed Mont Ventoux in 1336 just for the view — 450 years before anyone reached the top of Mont Blanc.

fact: Samuel Colt patented his revolver just ten days before the Alamo fell.

events.title: Texas declares independence from Mexico

events.title: The Alamo falls to Mexican troops

events.title: Darwin returns home on HMS Beagle

events.title: Victoria becomes Queen of the United Kingdom

fact: The Tale of Genji was being read in Japan by 1008 — decades before the real Macbeth became King of Scots.

fact: Hatshepsut's mummy was identified by a single tooth in June 2007 — the same month the first iPhone went on sale.

events.note: The planes took off from an aircraft carrier.

events.title: Paul McCartney is born
events.note: He was born in Liverpool.

events.title: Casablanca premieres in New York
events.note: Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman starred.

events.title: Jimi Hendrix is born
events.note: He was born in Seattle, Washington.

fact: Seabiscuit beat War Admiral in their famous match race just two days after Orson Welles's War of the Worlds broadcast.

events.title: Superman debuts in Action Comics
events.note: Jerry Siegel and Joe Shuster sold the rights for $130.

events.title: The Munich Agreement is signed
events.note: Britain and France let Germany annex the Sudetenland.

events.title: Orson Welles broadcasts The War of the Worlds
events.note: Newspapers claimed the radio play caused mass panic.

events.title: Seabiscuit beats War Admiral in a match race
events.note: About 40 million people listened on the radio.

events.title: A living coelacanth is caught off South Africa
events.note: The fish was thought to have died out with the dinosaurs.

fact: The barcode was patented in 1952 but first scanned at a till in June 1974, about six weeks before Nixon resigned.

events.title: The barcode is patented
events.note: Woodland got the idea drawing Morse code lines in beach sand.

events.title: The Terracotta Army is discovered
events.note: Farmers digging a well near Xi'an found it.

events.title: ABBA win Eurovision with 'Waterloo'
events.note: The contest was held in Brighton, England.

events.title: A barcode is scanned at a till
events.note: The item was a pack of Wrigley's gum in Troy, Ohio.

events.title: Richard Nixon resigns
events.note: He quit over the Watergate scandal.

fact: An African giraffe was presented at China's Ming court in 1414 — the year before England's archers won at Agincourt.

events.title: Timur dies on campaign to invade China
events.note: He fell ill near the Syr Darya and died in midwinter.

events.title: A giraffe is presented at the Ming court
events.note: Hailed as a qilin, a mythical beast of good omen.

events.title: Jan Hus is burned at the stake in Konstanz
events.note: The Czech reformer's death sparked the Hussite Wars.

events.title: Portugal captures Ceuta in North Africa
events.note: The start of Portugal's overseas empire.

events.title: English archers win the Battle of Agincourt
events.note: Longbowmen cut down heavily armoured French knights.

fact: When Akihito stepped down in April 2019, Japan's last emperor to abdicate had been Kōkaku, in 1817.

events.title: Japan's Emperor Kōkaku abdicates
events.note: He kept influence as a retired emperor for over 20 more years.

events.title: Japan's emperor renounces his divinity
events.note: Hirohito's statement is known as the Humanity Declaration.

events.title: Crown Prince Akihito marries a commoner, Michiko
events.note: Millions bought TV sets to watch the wedding parade.

events.title: Emperor Hirohito dies
events.note: He had reigned for over 62 years, the longest in Japan's history.

events.title: Japan's Emperor Akihito abdicates
events.note: A special law was passed to let him step down.

fact: England seized the Stone of Scone in 1296 and handed it back to Scotland in 1996 — 700 years later.

events.title: England seizes Scotland's Stone of Scone
events.note: It was built into a coronation chair at Westminster.

events.title: Robert the Bruce wins at Bannockburn
events.note: A decisive Scottish victory over the English.

events.title: Students steal the Stone of Scone
events.note: Four Glasgow students took it from Westminster Abbey.

events.title: Braveheart is released
events.note: Mel Gibson's epic won five Oscars including Best Picture.

events.title: The Stone of Scone returns to Scotland
events.note: It went on display in Edinburgh Castle.

fact: Tintin and Popeye are older than Vatican City: both debuted weeks before the treaty creating it was signed in 1929.

events.title: Tintin makes his debut
events.note: He first appeared in a Belgian newspaper supplement.

events.title: Popeye makes his debut
events.note: He first appeared in the comic strip Thimble Theatre.

events.title: The Lateran Treaty creates Vatican City
events.note: Mussolini's Italy signed it with the Holy See.

events.title: The St. Valentine's Day Massacre
events.note: Seven men were shot in a Chicago garage.

events.title: The first Academy Awards are presented
events.note: The ceremony lasted about 15 minutes.

fact: Cricket's "Timeless Test" was abandoned on 14 March 1939 so England could catch their boat home — the next day Germany seized Prague.

events.title: Don Bradman is born
events.note: He finished with a Test batting average of 99.94.

events.title: Cricket's "Timeless Test" is abandoned as a draw
events.note: The Durban match against South Africa had run for 12 days.

events.title: German troops occupy Prague
events.note: It broke the Munich Agreement made six months earlier.

events.title: Lou Gehrig gives his "luckiest man" speech
events.note: He was forced to retire by the disease now named after him.

events.title: Einstein signs a letter to Roosevelt about the atomic bomb
events.note: Leo Szilard drafted the warning about German nuclear research.

fact: Skylab fell to Earth just ten days after the Sony Walkman went on sale.

events.title: Sony is founded in Tokyo
events.note: It began as a radio repair shop in a Tokyo department store.

events.title: Margaret Thatcher becomes prime minister
events.note: She was Britain's first woman prime minister.

events.title: The Sony Walkman goes on sale
events.note: The blue-and-silver TPS-L2 cost ¥33,000.

events.title: Skylab falls back to Earth
events.note: Debris landed in Western Australia.

events.title: The Iran hostage crisis begins
events.note: Students seized the US embassy in Tehran.

fact: A Muslim geographer, al-Idrisi, made his famous world map in 1154 for Roger II, the Norman king of Sicily.

events.title: Normans capture Palermo
events.note: The city had been under Arab rule for over 200 years.

events.title: Roger II is crowned King of Sicily
events.note: The Norman kingdom mixed Latin, Greek and Arab cultures.

events.title: Al-Idrisi completes his world map
events.note: Its world map was engraved on a huge silver disc.

events.title: The Sicilian Vespers revolt erupts
events.note: It began with a riot at an Easter Monday church service.

events.title: Mercator publishes his world map projection
events.note: It kept compass bearings as straight lines for sailors.

fact: China's Qianlong Emperor abdicated in 1796 after 60 years, so as not to outreign his grandfather Kangxi, who died in 1722.

events.title: The Kangxi Dictionary is completed
events.note: It listed over 47,000 Chinese characters.

events.title: China's Kangxi Emperor dies after 61 years
events.note: The longest reign of any Chinese emperor.

events.title: China limits Western trade to Canton
events.note: Foreign merchants could deal only through licensed Chinese firms.

events.title: China's Qianlong Emperor abdicates
events.note: He handed the throne to his son but kept real power until he died.

events.title: Napoleon marries Joséphine de Beauharnais
events.note: Two days later he left Paris to command the army in Italy.

fact: Gold was found at Sutter's Mill nine days before Mexico signed California over to the US — neither side knew.

events.title: Gold is found at Sutter's Mill, California
events.note: James Marshall spotted flakes in the mill's tailrace.

events.title: The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo is signed
events.note: Mexico ceded California and much of the Southwest.

events.title: Revolution in Paris forces the French king to abdicate
events.note: Louis Philippe fled to England; France became a republic.

events.title: The Seneca Falls women's rights convention opens
events.note: It launched the US campaign for women's suffrage.

events.title: Gold is struck in the Klondike
events.note: It set off a stampede to Canada's Yukon.

fact: Opera giants Wagner and Verdi were born in the same year — 1813, when Pride and Prejudice came out.

events.title: Pride and Prejudice is published
events.note: It appeared anonymously, 'by the author of Sense and Sensibility'.

events.title: Richard Wagner is born in Leipzig
events.note: He later wrote the four-opera Ring cycle.

events.title: Giuseppe Verdi is born
events.note: Born in a village near Busseto, in the Duchy of Parma.

events.title: Richard Wagner dies in Venice
events.note: He died of a heart attack at the Palazzo Vendramin.

events.title: Giuseppe Verdi dies in Milan
events.note: His last opera, Falstaff, had premiered eight years earlier.

fact: Britain took Sri Lanka's last kingdom, Kandy, by treaty just four days after Napoleon escaped from Elba.

events.title: Britain and the US sign the Treaty of Ghent
events.note: It ended the War of 1812 — though news travelled slowly.

events.title: Andrew Jackson wins the Battle of New Orleans
events.note: It was fought after the peace treaty had been signed.

events.title: Napoleon escapes from exile on Elba
events.note: He sailed for France with about 1,000 men.

events.title: The Kingdom of Kandy is ceded to Britain
events.note: The Kandyan Convention ended 2,000 years of Sinhalese kingship.

events.title: Jane Austen's Emma is published
events.note: It was dedicated, reluctantly, to the Prince Regent.

fact: Pokémon Red and Green came out in Japan just over four months before Dolly the sheep was born.

events.title: Nintendo's Game Boy goes on sale in Japan
events.note: It came bundled with Tetris abroad.

events.title: Toy Story opens in US cinemas
events.note: It was the first fully computer-animated feature.

events.title: Pokémon Red and Green are released
events.note: Satoshi Tajiri was inspired by his insect collecting.

events.title: Dolly the sheep is born
events.note: She was the first mammal cloned from an adult cell.

events.title: Google is incorporated
events.note: It was run from a garage in Menlo Park.

fact: The Vatican admitted it was wrong to condemn Galileo on 31 Oct 1992 — three days before Bill Clinton was elected.

events.title: Construction of the Taj Mahal begins
events.note: Shah Jahan built it as a tomb for his wife.

events.title: Galileo is convicted by the Inquisition
events.note: He spent his last years under house arrest.

events.title: The Maastricht Treaty is signed
events.note: It created the European Union.

events.title: The Pope admits the Church erred over Galileo
events.note: It came 359 years after his trial.

events.title: Bill Clinton is elected US president
events.note: He beat George H. W. Bush and Ross Perot.

fact: Before the Visigoths in AD 410, no foreign enemy had taken Rome for about 800 years — since the Gauls, c. 390 BC.

events.title: Gauls sack Rome
events.note: Legend says the sacred geese of Juno raised the alarm.

events.title: Work begins on Rome's Aurelian Walls
events.note: Large stretches of the walls still stand.

events.title: Visigoths sack Rome
events.note: Alaric's army looted the city for three days.

events.title: A Christian mob murders Hypatia in Alexandria
events.note: She was a celebrated mathematician and astronomer.

events.title: Italian troops capture Rome from the Pope
events.note: They broke through the Aurelian Walls at Porta Pia.

fact: When work began on Abu Simbel around 1264 BC, Egypt's first pyramid, Djoser's, was already about 1,400 years old.

events.title: Egypt's first pyramid is built for King Djoser
events.note: It was designed by his architect Imhotep, using six stacked steps.

events.title: Work begins on Ramesses II's temples at Abu Simbel
events.note: They were carved straight into a sandstone cliff by the Nile.

events.title: Burckhardt spots the buried temple of Abu Simbel
events.note: Only the top of the facade showed above the sand.

events.title: Belzoni digs his way into the Great Temple of Abu Simbel
events.note: The Italian strongman spent 22 days clearing sand from the entrance.

events.title: The Grand Egyptian Museum officially opens near Giza
events.note: It cost an estimated $1.2 billion.
